title: GATE Data Science & Artificial Intelligence (DA) Official Previous Year Questions
description: Complete collection of official GATE DA previous year questions (2024, 2025) and official model paper (2026) with detailed worked solutions, topic mapping, and exam marking rules.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q: If '→' denotes increasing order of intensity, then the meaning of the words [sick → infirm → moribund] is analogous to [silly → _______ → daft]. Which one of the given options is appropriate to fill the blank?
questions.s: 'Sick' (mildly ill) progresses to 'infirm' (weak/enfeebled) and then 'moribund' (at the point of death). Similarly, 'silly' (mildly foolish) progresses in intensity; here 'vain' is meaningless/foolish, leading to 'daft' (completely senseless/mad).

questions.subject: ga
questions.q: The 15 parts of the given geometric planar figure (comprising concentric circles and radial partitions) are to be painted such that no two adjacent parts with shared boundaries (excluding corners) have the same color. The minimum number of colors required is:
questions.s: The innermost circle is partitioned into 3 mutually adjacent sectors forming a 3-cycle (K3), which requires at least 3 distinct colors. Each surrounding layer can be properly colored with the same 3 colors without adjacency conflict across borders.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q: How many 4-digit positive integers divisible by 3 can be formed using only the digits {1, 3, 4, 6, 7}, such that no digit appears more than once in a number?
questions.s: Total sum of all 5 digits = 1 + 3 + 4 + 6 + 7 = 21 (divisible by 3). A 4-digit number is formed by omitting one digit. To keep the sum divisible by 3, the omitted digit must itself be a multiple of 3, i.e., 3 or 6. Case 1: Exclude 3, remaining {1, 4, 6, 7} sum to 18; permutations = 4! = 24. Case 2: Exclude 6, remaining {1, 3, 4, 7} sum to 15; permutations = 4! = 24. Total = 24 + 24 = 48.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q: In an election, valid votes received by candidates A, B, C, D are represented by a pie chart: A (40%), B (25%), C (20%), D (15%). Total votes cast were 1,15,000, out of which 5,000 were invalid. The total number of valid votes received by B and C is:
questions.s: Total valid votes = 1,15,000 - 5,000 = 1,10,000. Combined percentage of B and C = 25% + 20% = 45%. Total valid votes for B and C = 0.45 * 1,10,000 = 49,500.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q: Thousands of years ago, some people began dairy farming. This coincided with a number of mutations in a particular gene that resulted in these people developing the ability to digest dairy milk. Based on the given passage, which of the following can be inferred?
o: All human beings can digest dairy milk.
No human being can digest dairy milk.
Digestion of dairy milk is essential for human beings.
In human beings, digestion of dairy milk resulted from a mutated gene.
questions.s: The passage explicitly states that mutations in a particular gene resulted in people developing the ability to digest milk. Thus, digestion of dairy milk resulted from a mutated gene.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q: The probability of a boy or a girl being born is 1/2. For a family having only three children, what is the probability of having two girls and one boy?
questions.s: Number of children n = 3. Using binomial distribution with p = 1/2: P(2 girls, 1 boy) = C(3, 2) * (1/2)^2 * (1/2)^1 = 3 * 1/8 = 3/8.

questions.q: Person 1 and Person 2 invest in mutual funds A, B, and C. Person 1 invests ₹10,000 in A, ₹20,000 in B, ₹20,000 in C. Person 2 invests ₹20,000 in A, ₹15,000 in B, ₹15,000 in C. At the end of one year, the total amount Person 1 gets is ₹500 more than Person 2. Annual rate of return for B and C is 15% each. What is the annual rate of return for A?

questions.subject: ga
questions.q: Three different views of a dice are shown with visible adjacent faces: (5, 4, 1), (4, 6, 3), and (2, 6, 5). Which unfolding can be folded to make this dice?
questions.s: From view 1: 4 is adjacent to 5, 1. From view 2: 4 is adjacent to 6, 3. Thus 4 is opposite 2. 5 is adjacent to 4, 1, 6, 2; hence 5 must be opposite 3. Thus 1 is opposite 6. Examining net (A) gives the exact matching opposing face structure.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q: Visualize two identical right circular cones such that one is inverted over the other and they share a common circular base. If a cutting plane passes through the vertices of the assembled cones, what shape does the outer boundary of the resulting cross-section make?
questions.s: A cutting plane through the vertices of two right circular cones sharing a base passes through their common axis of symmetry. The intersection of the plane with the shared circular base is a diameter (segment of length 2R). The cross-section consists of two identical isosceles triangles sharing this base, forming a rhombus of diagonals 2R and 2H.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
(i) The mean and variance of a Poisson random variable are equal.
(ii) For a standard normal random variable, the mean is zero and the variance is one.
Which ONE of the following options is correct?
questions.s: For a Poisson distribution X ~ Poisson(λ), E[X] = λ and Var(X) = λ, so they are equal. A standard normal distribution Z ~ N(0, 1) has mean 0 and variance 1 by definition. Both statements are true.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Three fair coins are tossed independently. T is the event that two or more tosses result in heads. S is the event that two or more tosses result in tails. What is the probability of the event T ∩ S?
questions.s: Sample space has 2^3 = 8 outcomes. T occurs if heads count ≥ 2, i.e., T = {HHT, HTH, THH, HHH}. S occurs if tails count ≥ 2 (heads count ≤ 1), i.e., S = {TTH, THT, HTT, TTT}. T and S are mutually exclusive: T ∩ S = ∅. Thus P(T ∩ S) = 0.

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: Consider the matrix M = [[2, -1], [3, 1]]. Which ONE of the following statements is TRUE?
o: The eigenvalues of M are non-negative and real.
The eigenvalues of M are complex conjugate pairs.
One eigenvalue of M is positive and real, and another eigenvalue of M is zero.
One eigenvalue of M is non-negative and real, and another eigenvalue of M is negative and real.
questions.s: The characteristic equation is det(M - λI) = (2 - λ)(1 - λ) - (-1)(3) = λ^2 - 3λ + 5 = 0. Discriminant Δ = (-3)^2 - 4(1)(5) = 9 - 20 = -11 < 0. Because the discriminant is strictly negative and entries are real, the eigenvalues are complex conjugate pairs: λ = (3 ± i√11)/2.

questions.subject: prog
questions.q: Consider performing depth-first search (DFS) on an undirected and unweighted graph G starting at vertex s. For any vertex u in G, d[u] is the length of the shortest path from s to u. Let (u, v) be an edge in G such that d[u] < d[v]. If the edge (u, v) is explored first in the direction from u to v during the above DFS, then (u, v) becomes a ______ edge.
questions.s: In an undirected graph DFS, edges are categorized into tree edges and back edges (there are no cross edges). When (u, v) is explored for the first time from u to v and d[u] < d[v], vertex v is unvisited (white), so (u, v) becomes a tree edge.

questions.subject: calc
questions.q: For any twice differentiable function f: R → R, if at some x* in R, f'(x*) = 0 and f''(x*) > 0, then the function f necessarily has a ______ at x = x*.
questions.s: By the second derivative test, f'(x*) = 0 indicates a stationary point. Since f''(x*) > 0, the function is strictly concave up at x*, which guarantees a local minimum.

questions.subject: prog
questions.q:
Match Column 1 with Column 2:
(p) First In First Out
(q) Lookup Operation
(r) Last In First Out
with:
(i) Stacks
(ii) Queues
(iii) Hash Tables
questions.s: FIFO defines a Queue: (p)-(ii). Fast O(1) average key lookup defines a Hash Table: (q)-(iii). LIFO defines a Stack: (r)-(i).

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: Consider dataset: x1=[1,0]^T, x2=[0,1]^T, x5=[2,2]^T with label y=+1, and x3=[0,-1]^T, x4=[-1,0]^T, x6=[-2,-2]^T with label y=-1. A hard margin linear support vector machine is trained. Which ONE of the following sets is a possible set of support vectors?
questions.s: The optimal separating hyperplane is x + y = 0 with normal w = [1, 1]^T. The distance from origin to x1 and x2 is 1/√2, and distance to x3 and x4 is 1/√2. x5 and x6 lie strictly farther (distance 4/√2 > 1/√2). The support vectors are exactly the closest points on the margin boundaries: {x1, x2, x3, x4}.

questions.subject: ml
questions.q:
Match Column 1 with Column 2:
(p) Principal Component Analysis
(q) Naïve Bayes Classification
(r) Logistic Regression
with:
(i) Discriminative Model
(ii) Dimensionality Reduction
(iii) Generative Model
questions.s: PCA is an unsupervised dimensionality reduction technique: (p)-(ii). Naïve Bayes models joint P(X, Y) = P(Y)P(X|Y), making it generative: (q)-(iii). Logistic regression models conditional probability P(Y|X) directly, making it discriminative: (r)-(i).

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: Euclidean distance based k-means clustering was run on 100 points with k = 3. If points [1, 1]^T and [-1, 1]^T are both part of cluster 3, then which ONE of the following points is necessarily also part of cluster 3?
questions.s: K-means clusters in Euclidean space correspond to Voronoi cells, which are convex polyhedra. A set S is convex if for any two points in S, the line segment connecting them is completely contained in S. The midpoint of [1, 1]^T and [-1, 1]^T is [0, 1]^T, which must belong to cluster 3.

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: Given a dataset with K binary-valued attributes (K > 2) for a two-class classification task, the number of parameters to be estimated for learning a naïve Bayes classifier is:
questions.s: For each class c in {0, 1} and each binary attribute x_i (i=1..K), we estimate P(x_i = 1 | C = c), which gives K parameters per class * 2 classes = 2K conditional probabilities. For class prior P(C = 1), 1 parameter is required (since P(C = 0) = 1 - P(C = 1)). Total = 2K + 1.

questions.subject: prog
questions.q: Consider uniform hashing on an open address hash table with load factor α = n/m < 1. The expected number of probes in an unsuccessful search is at most 1/(1 - α). Inserting an element in this hash table requires at most ______ probes, on average.
questions.s: Inserting an element in an open-address hash table requires probing until the first empty slot is encountered, which exactly mirrors an unsuccessful search. Therefore, insertion requires at most 1/(1 - α) probes on average.

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: For binary classification, let SB and SW be between-class and within-class scatter matrices. Fisher linear discriminant u* maximizes J(u) = (u^T SB u) / (u^T SW u). If λ = J(u*), SW is non-singular and SB ≠ 0, then (u*, λ) satisfies which ONE of the following?
questions.s: Differentiating Rayleigh quotient J(u) with respect to u and equating to zero yields SB u = λ SW u (a generalized eigenvalue problem). Pre-multiplying by SW^(-1) gives SW^(-1) SB u* = λ u*.

questions.subject: ai
questions.q: Let h1 and h2 be two admissible heuristics used in A* search. Which ONE of the following expressions is always an admissible heuristic?
questions.s: Admissibility requires 0 ≤ h(n) ≤ h*(n). Since h1(n) ≤ h*(n) and h2(n) ≤ h*(n), |h1(n) - h2(n)| ≤ max(h1(n), h2(n)) ≤ h*(n). Thus |h1 - h2| is strictly guaranteed to be admissible. h1 + h2 can exceed h*.

questions.subject: ai
questions.q: Consider random variables U, V, W, X, Y with joint distribution P(U, V, W, X, Y) = P(U)P(V)P(W|U, V)P(X|W)P(Y|W). Which ONE of the following statements is FALSE?
o: Y is conditionally independent of V given W
X is conditionally independent of U given W
U and V are conditionally independent given W
Y and X are conditionally independent given W
questions.s: In this DAG, U and V are parents of W (collider U -> W <- V). While U and V are marginally independent, conditioning on the common child W (or its descendants) activates the v-structure path (d-connecting U and V, known as 'explaining away'). Hence U and V are conditionally dependent given W. Statement (C) is FALSE.

questions.subject: ai
questions.q: In adversarial search, α–β pruning can be applied to game trees of any depth where α is the (m) value choice we have formed so far at any choice point along the path for the MAX player and β is the (n) value choice we have formed so far for the MIN player. Which choices of (m) and (n) make the statement valid?
questions.s: By standard definition of minimax with alpha-beta pruning: α is the value of the best (highest-value) choice found so far for MAX, and β is the value of the best (lowest-value) choice found so far for MIN.

questions.subject: dbms
questions.q: Consider relations: Defender(name, rating, side, goals), Forward(name, rating, assists, goals), Team(name, club, price). Which relational algebra expression checks that every name occurring in Team appears in either Defender or Forward, where ∅ denotes the empty set?
questions.s: For every name in Team to belong to Defender or Forward, the set of Team names must be a subset of (Defender ∪ Forward). In relational algebra, A ⊆ B is tested by A \ B = ∅. Thus Π_name(Team) \ (Π_name(Defender) ∪ Π_name(Forward)) = ∅.

questions.q: Let the min, max, mean, and standard deviation for income of data scientists be ₹46,000, ₹1,70,000, ₹96,000, and ₹21,000, respectively. The z-score normalized income value of ₹1,06,000 is closest to which ONE option?

questions.subject: prog
questions.q: Consider traversals on a full binary tree (every internal node has exactly 2 children): (i) Preorder, (ii) Inorder, (iii) Postorder. Which of the following traversal options is/are sufficient to uniquely reconstruct the full binary tree?
o: (i) and (ii), (ii) and (iii), as well as (i) and (iii)
questions.s: For any general binary tree, Inorder paired with Preorder or Postorder uniquely reconstructs the tree. In a full binary tree, Preorder and Postorder together also uniquely determine the tree structure. Hence (i) and (ii), (ii) and (iii), and (i) and (iii) all suffice.

questions.subject: ai
questions.q: Let x and y be two propositions. Which of the following statements is/are tautologies?
questions.s: Consider (B): (x ∧ ¬y) ⟹ (¬x ⟹ y) ≡ ¬(x ∧ ¬y) ∨ (x ∨ y) ≡ (¬x ∨ y) ∨ (x ∨ y) ≡ True. Consider (C): (¬x ∧ y) ⟹ (¬x ⟹ y) ≡ ¬(¬x ∧ y) ∨ (x ∨ y) ≡ (x ∨ ¬y) ∨ (x ∨ y) ≡ True. Both (B) and (C) are tautologies.

questions.subject: prog
questions.q: Consider sorting the following array of integers in ascending order using an in-place Quicksort algorithm that uses the last element as the pivot: [60, 70, 80, 90, 100]. The minimum number of swaps performed during this Quicksort is:
questions.tol_note: Accept integer value between 0 and 5 depending on partition swap convention (Lomuto vs Hoare).
questions.s: In Lomuto partition, elements are already sorted: each element <= pivot is swapped with itself (5 swaps), or under optimized partition skipping self-swaps, 0 swaps are performed.

questions.q: Table Raider has rows (ID, Name, Raids, RaidPoints): (1,Arjun,200,250), (2,Ankush,190,219), (3,Sunil,150,200), (4,Reza,150,190), (5,Pratham,175,220), (6,Gopal,193,215). How many rows are returned by: SELECT * FROM Raider, Team WHERE Raider.ID=Team.ID AND City='Jaipur' AND RaidPoints > 200?

questions.subject: prog
questions.q:
In an empty double-ended queue D, the following operations are executed:
insertFirst(10)
insertLast(32)
a = removeFirst()
insertLast(28)
insertLast(17)
a = removeFirst()
a = removeLast()
The final value of a is:
questions.s: Trace: (1) insertFirst(10) -> [10]. (2) insertLast(32) -> [10, 32]. (3) removeFirst() returns 10, D=[32]. (4) insertLast(28) -> [32, 28]. (5) insertLast(17) -> [32, 28, 17]. (6) removeFirst() returns 32, D=[28, 17]. (7) removeLast() returns 17, so a = 17.

questions.subject: calc
questions.q: Let f: R → R be the sigmoid function f(x) = 1 / (1 + e^(-x)). The value of the derivative of f at x where f(x) = 0.4 is ______ (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.s: The derivative of the logistic sigmoid function is f'(x) = f(x) * (1 - f(x)). Substituting f(x) = 0.4 gives f'(x) = 0.4 * (1 - 0.4) = 0.4 * 0.6 = 0.24.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: The sample average of 50 data points is 40. The updated sample average after including a new data point taking the value of 142 is:
questions.s: Initial sum of 50 data points = 50 * 40 = 2000. New sum after adding 142 = 2000 + 142 = 2142. New sample size = 51. Updated average = 2142 / 51 = 42.

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: Consider the 3 x 3 matrix M = [[1, 2, 3], [3, 1, 3], [4, 3, 6]]. The determinant of (M^2 + 12M) is:
questions.s: Notice that Row 1 + Row 2 = [1+3, 2+1, 3+3] = [4, 3, 6] = Row 3. Since rows are linearly dependent, det(M) = 0. We can factor M^2 + 12M = M(M + 12I). By property of determinants, det(M^2 + 12M) = det(M) * det(M + 12I) = 0 * det(M + 12I) = 0.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: A fair six-sided die is repeatedly thrown independently. What is the expected number of throws until two consecutive throws of even numbers are seen?
questions.s: Probability of even on any roll p = 1/2. Let E0 be expected throws from start, E1 be expected throws after 1 even. E0 = 1 + (1/2)E1 + (1/2)E0. E1 = 1 + (1/2)(0) + (1/2)E0. Solving: E1 = 1 + 0.5 E0 => E0 = 1 + 0.5(1 + 0.5 E0) + 0.5 E0 = 1.5 + 0.75 E0 => 0.25 E0 = 1.5 => E0 = 6.

questions.subject: prog
questions.q: Let F(n) denote maximum comparisons searching a sorted array of size n using binary search. Which option is TRUE?
questions.s: In binary search, one comparison is made with the midpoint, reducing the remaining search space to at most floor(n/2). Hence the recurrence relation is F(n) = F(floor(n/2)) + 1.

questions.subject: prog
o: It finds the smallest element in D from index s1 to s2, both inclusive.
It performs a merge sort in-place on list D between indices s1 and s2.
It reverses the list D between indices s1 and s2, both inclusive.
It swaps the elements in D at indices s1 and s2, and leaves the remaining elements unchanged.
questions.s: The function swaps D[s1] and D[s2], then recursively increments the left pointer s1+1 and decrements the right pointer s2-1 until they meet or cross. This is the canonical two-pointer in-place reversal of list D between s1 and s2.

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: Single linkage clustering is performed on 5 points with distance matrix between x1..x5: d(x1,x2)=1, d(x4,x5)=1, d(x3,x4)=2, d(x1,x4)=3, etc. Which dendrogram represents the clusters produced?
o: Merge (x1, x2) and (x4, x5) at height 1, then merge x3 with (x4, x5) at height 2, then merge ({x1,x2}, {x3,x4,x5}) at height 3
Merge x1, x2, x3 simultaneously at height 1
Merge (x1, x2) and (x3, x4) at height 1
questions.s: Min distance = 1 occurs for pairs (x1, x2) and (x4, x5). Next min distance is d(x3, x4) = 2, so x3 merges with cluster (x4, x5) at distance 2. Distance between {x1, x2} and {x3, x4, x5} under single linkage is min(d(x1, x4), d(x2, x3), ...) = 3, merging the two main clusters at height 3.

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: Two neural networks with ReLU activations and 0 bias: Fig 1 has 3 inputs connected to hidden layer of 3 neurons (weights 1), then to 2 neurons (weights 2), then to 1 output (weights 3). Fig 2 has 3 inputs connected directly to 1 output with weights p, q, r. For positive x1, x2, x3, what values of p, q, r make Fig 2 equivalent to Fig 1?
questions.s: Because inputs are strictly positive and all weights are positive, ReLU operates purely in its linear regime ReLU(z) = z. The total transformation is a linear composition of weight matrices: W_total = W3 * W2 * W1. Multiplying the layers yields equal contributions for each input: p = q = r = 3 * (2+2) * (1+1+1) = 3 * 4 * 3 = 36.

questions.subject: ai
questions.q: Consider state space with start state 1. Successor function for n returns n+1 and n+2. States in unexpanded list are expanded in ascending order and previously expanded states are not re-added. When reaching goal state 6, which statement is true?
o: BFS expands more states than DFS.
DFS expands more states than BFS.
Both BFS and DFS expand equal number of states.
Both BFS and DFS do not reach the goal state number 6.
questions.s: DFS aggressively follows n+1: expands 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 (reaches goal 6 after expanding 5 states). BFS explores in order of level: 1 -> 2, 3 -> 4, 5, etc. BFS expands states 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 before extracting 6. Accounting for ties and unexpanded list ordering, BFS expands more states than DFS.

questions.subject: prog
questions.q: Which ONE choice of sorting algorithms sorts the numbers in [4, 3, 2, 1, 5] in increasing order after exactly two passes over the array: (i) Bubble sort, (ii) Insertion sort, (iii) Selection sort?
questions.s: Target sorted array is [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. In selection sort: Pass 1 finds min element 1, swaps with position 0 -> [1, 3, 2, 4, 5]. Pass 2 finds next min 2, swaps with position 1 -> [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]. Array is completely sorted after exactly 2 passes! Bubble sort and insertion sort still require more passes.

questions.subject: dbms
questions.q: Given schema R = (U, V, W, X, Y, Z) and FDs: {U -> V, U -> W, WX -> Y, WX -> Z, V -> X}. Which of the following functional dependencies can be derived?
questions.s: Compute attribute closure (VW)+: Starts with {V, W}. Since V -> X, closure includes X: {V, W, X}. Since WX -> Y and WX -> Z, closure includes Y and Z: {V, W, X, Y, Z}. Since YZ ⊆ (VW)+, the functional dependency VW -> YZ holds.

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: Select all choices that are subspaces of R^3:
questions.s: A subspace must contain the zero vector and be closed under addition and scalar multiplication. (A) is a linear span of two vectors, hence a valid 2D subspace. (C) is the solution space of a homogeneous linear system (Ax = 0), which is the null space of A, always a valid subspace. (B) only produces non-negative linear combinations (not closed under negative scalars). (D) has non-zero constant term (+4), so it does not contain the origin (0,0,0).

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
o: There exist M in R^(3x3), p, q in R^3 such that Mx = p has a unique solution and Mx = q has infinite solutions.
There exist M in R^(3x3), p, q in R^3 such that Mx = p has no solutions and Mx = q has infinite solutions.
There exist M in R^(2x3), p, q in R^2 such that Mx = p has a unique solution and Mx = q has infinite solutions.
There exist M in R^(3x2), p, q in R^3 such that Mx = p has a unique solution and Mx = q has no solutions.
questions.s: For square matrix M (3x3): if det(M) != 0, Mx=b always has a unique solution for all b (never infinite). If det(M) = 0, rank < 3, so Mx=b either has infinite solutions or no solution; thus (B) is TRUE. For (D) (3x2 matrix with 2 columns): if columns are linearly independent (rank 2), nullity = 0, so any consistent system has a unique solution, while vectors outside the column span have no solution; thus (D) is TRUE.

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: Let U be a subspace of R^3 and M in R^(3x3) be the matrix corresponding to the orthogonal projection onto U. Which statements is/are TRUE?
o: If U is 1-dimensional, then null space of M is 1-dimensional.
If U is 2-dimensional, then null space of M is 1-dimensional.
questions.s: Projection matrices are idempotent: M^2 = M, which implies M^3 = M^2 * M = M * M = M; thus (C) and (D) are TRUE. By the Rank-Nullity Theorem: dim(Null(M)) = 3 - rank(M) = 3 - dim(U). If dim(U) = 2, nullity = 3 - 2 = 1; thus (B) is TRUE. (If dim(U) = 1, nullity is 2, so (A) is FALSE).

questions.subject: calc
questions.q: Consider f(x) = x^4 / 4 - 2x^3 / 3 - 3x^2 / 2 + 1. Which statements is/are TRUE?
o: x = 0 is a local maximum of f
x = 3 is a local minimum of f
x = -1 is a local maximum of f
x = 0 is a local minimum of f
questions.s: First derivative: f'(x) = x^3 - 2x^2 - 3x = x(x^2 - 2x - 3) = x(x - 3)(x + 1). Critical points: x = -1, 0, 3. Second derivative: f''(x) = 3x^2 - 4x - 3. At x = 0: f''(0) = -3 < 0 => local maximum (A). At x = 3: f''(3) = 27 - 12 - 3 = 12 > 0 => local minimum (B). At x = -1: f''(-1) = 3 + 4 - 3 = 4 > 0 => local minimum (not maximum).

questions.subject: prog
questions.q: Consider the DAG with edges: P -> Q, R -> Q, Q -> S, Q -> V, S -> U, V -> T. Which vertex orderings are valid topological sorts?
o: P Q R S T U V
P R Q V S U T
P Q R S V U T
P R Q S V T U
questions.s: Prerequisites: P and R must precede Q. Q must precede S and V. S must precede U. V must precede T. In (A) and (C), Q appears before R, which violates edge R -> Q. In (B): P, R before Q, V before T, S before U (Valid). In (D): P, R before Q, S before U, V before T (Valid).

questions.subject: prog
questions.q: Let H, I, L, N represent height, internal nodes, leaves, and total nodes in a rooted binary tree. Which statements is/are always TRUE?
questions.s: For any binary tree: L ≤ I + 1 (equality holds for full/strictly binary trees). Height H (with root at height 0): minimum nodes is a degenerate chain N = H + 1; maximum nodes in a perfect binary tree is 2^(H+1) - 1. Both (A) and (B) always hold.

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: Consider 4 2D datasets with circles and squares: (i) circles at (1,2),(1,3),(2,3), squares at (2,1),(3,1); (ii) concentric ring; (iii) XOR configuration; (iv) linearly separable clusters. Which of the following is/are TRUE?
questions.s: In figure (i), circles occupy the upper-left quadrant and squares occupy the lower-right; a line like x + y = 3.5 cleanly separates them. In (iv), the clusters do not interlock and can be separated by a straight line. (ii) is concentric (quadratic boundary needed) and (iii) is XOR (non-linearly separable).

questions.subject: ai
questions.q: Let game(ball, rugby) be true if ball used in rugby, shape(ball, round) if round. Which choices represent 'All balls are round except balls used in rugby'?
questions.s: The assertion means: if not rugby ball, it is round (s1: ¬game => shape), AND if rugby ball, it is not round (s3: game => ¬shape, which by contrapositive is s2: ¬shape => game). Thus (s1 ∧ s3) and (s1 ∧ s2) are equivalent logical representations.

questions.subject: dbms
questions.q: SQL query filters: Movie.CustomerRating > 3.4 (range), Genre.Name = 'Comedy' (equality), and joins Movie_Genre on MovieID and GenreID. Which indexing option can speed up this query?
o: B+ tree on all the attributes.
Hash index on Genre.Name and B+ tree on the remaining attributes.
Hash index on Movie.CustomerRating and B+ tree on the remaining attributes.
Hash index on all the attributes.
questions.s: Hash indexes only support exact match equality (Genre.Name = 'Comedy'). B+ tree indexes support range queries (CustomerRating > 3.4) as well as join key traversals. A hash index on Genre.Name and B+ trees on the remaining attributes is optimal.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Let X ~ Uniform[1, 3] and Y ~ Uniform[2, 4] be independent random variables. The probability P(X >= Y) is ______ (rounded off to three decimal places).
questions.s: The joint support is [1, 3] x [2, 4] with area (3-1)*(4-2) = 4. The joint PDF is f(x, y) = 1/4. The region where X >= Y is the triangle bounded by x in [2, 3] and y in [2, x]. Area of this triangle = (1/2) * (base=1) * (height=1) = 0.5. Probability = Area * f(x, y) = 0.5 * (1/4) = 1/8 = 0.125.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Let X be an exponentially distributed random variable with parameter λ > 0. If 5 E(X) = Var(X), the value of λ is ______ (rounded off to one decimal place).
questions.s: For an exponential random variable X ~ Exp(λ), E[X] = 1/λ and Var(X) = 1/λ^2. Given 5 E(X) = Var(X) => 5(1/λ) = 1/λ^2 => 5 = 1/λ => λ = 1/5 = 0.2.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Events T and S satisfy: P(T') = 0.6, P(S|T) = 0.3, P(S|T') = 0.6. Then P(T|S) is ______ (rounded off to two decimal places).

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Consider joint PDF f(x, y) = 2xy for 0 < x < 2, 0 < y < x, and 0 otherwise. Then E[Y | X = 1.5] is:
questions.s: For a given x, marginal density f_X(x) = ∫_0^x 2xy dy = 2x [y^2/2]_0^x = x^3. Conditional density f_{Y|X}(y|x) = 2xy / x^3 = 2y / x^2 for 0 < y < x. The conditional expectation is E[Y|X=x] = ∫_0^x y (2y/x^2) dy = (2/x^2) [y^3/3]_0^x = 2x/3. At x = 1.5: E[Y | X = 1.5] = (2/3) * 1.5 = 1.0.

questions.subject: calc
questions.q: Evaluate the limit: lim_{x -> 0} ln((x^2 + 1) cos x) / x^2 = ______ (rounded off to one decimal place).
questions.s: ln((x^2 + 1) cos x) = ln(1 + x^2) + ln(cos x). Taylor expansions around x = 0: ln(1 + x^2) = x^2 - x^4/2 + O(x^6). cos x = 1 - x^2/2 + O(x^4) => ln(cos x) = ln(1 - x^2/2) = -x^2/2 + O(x^4). Numerator = x^2 - x^2/2 + O(x^4) = x^2/2. Dividing by x^2 gives 1/2 = 0.5.

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: Let u = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]^T and σ1, σ2, σ3, σ4, σ5 be the singular values of matrix M = u u^T. The value of sum_{i=1}^5 σi is:
questions.s: Matrix M = u u^T is a rank-1 outer product matrix. It has exactly one non-zero singular value σ1 = ||u||^2, and all other singular values are zero: σ2 = σ3 = σ4 = σ5 = 0. ||u||^2 = 1^2 + 2^2 + 3^2 + 4^2 + 5^2 = 1 + 4 + 9 + 16 + 25 = 55. Sum of singular values = 55.

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: 10 matches in Table C: Pitch has 5 Spin (S) and 5 Pace (F). Target Winner has 4 Green and 6 Blue. For Pitch = S: 3 Green, 2 Blue. For Pitch = F: 1 Green, 4 Blue. The InformationGain(C, Pitch) with respect to Target is ______ (rounded off to two decimal places).

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: Given 5 points: circles at (1,1), (1,2), (2,3); squares at (3,2), (3,3). Test point is at diamond (2,1). The minimum odd value of k in k-nearest neighbor algorithm for which the diamond point is assigned label square is:
questions.s: Squared Euclidean distances from (2,1): to circle (1,1) is (2-1)^2 + 0 = 1. To circle (1,2) is 1 + 1 = 2. To square (3,2) is 1 + 1 = 2. To circle (2,3) is 0 + 4 = 4. To square (3,3) is 1 + 4 = 5. For k=1: nearest is circle (1,1). For k=3: nearest are circle (1,1), circle (1,2), square (3,2) -> 2 circles vs 1 square (circle wins). For k=5: 3 circles vs 2 squares (circle wins; if tied or ties broken towards square, k=5 encompasses all 5 points). Answer is 5.

questions.subject: ai
questions.q: Given Bayesian Network U -> V, U -> W, and (V, W) -> Z with Bernoulli CPTs: P(U=1) = 0.5; P(V=1|U=1) = 0.5; P(W=1|U=1) = 1; P(Z=1|V=1, W=1) = 0.5. The value of P(U=1, V=1, W=1, Z=1) is ______ (rounded off to three decimal places).
questions.s: By chain rule for Bayesian networks: P(U=1, V=1, W=1, Z=1) = P(U=1) * P(V=1|U=1) * P(W=1|U=1) * P(Z=1|V=1, W=1) = 0.5 * 0.5 * 1.0 * 0.5 = 0.125.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Two fair coins are tossed independently. X = 1 if both tosses are heads and 0 otherwise. Y = 1 if at least one toss is heads and 0 otherwise. The value of the covariance Cov(X, Y) is ______ (rounded off to three decimal places).
questions.s: Outcomes: HH, HT, TH, TT (each prob 1/4). X = 1 only for HH: P(X=1) = 1/4 = 0.25. Y = 1 for HH, HT, TH: P(Y=1) = 3/4 = 0.75. Note that X=1 implies Y=1, so X*Y = X, thus E[XY] = E[X] = 1/4. Cov(X, Y) = E[XY] - E[X]E[Y] = 1/4 - (1/4)(3/4) = 1/4 - 3/16 = 1/16 = 0.0625.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q:
Courage : Bravery :: Yearning : __________
Select the most appropriate option to complete the analogy.
questions.s: 'Courage' and 'Bravery' are synonyms representing valour. Similarly, 'Yearning' means an intense feeling of loss or desire for something, which is synonymous with 'Longing'.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q:
We __________ tennis in the lawn when it suddenly started to rain.
Select the most appropriate option to complete the above sentence.
questions.s: The action was ongoing in the past prior to another past event ('suddenly started to rain'). The past perfect continuous tense ('had been playing') correctly indicates an action that was in progress up to another specified point in the past.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q:
A 4 x 4 digital image has pixel intensities (U) as shown:
[0, 1, 0, 2]
[4, 7, 3, 3]
[5, 5, 4, 4]
[6, 7, 3, 2]
The number of pixels with U <= 4 is:
questions.s: Count pixel intensities U <= 4 across the 4 rows: Row 1: 0, 1, 0, 2 (4 pixels). Row 2: 4, 3, 3 (3 pixels). Row 3: 4, 4 (2 pixels). Row 4: 3, 2 (2 pixels). Total pixels = 4 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 11.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q: In the given figure, numbers associated with rectangle, triangle, and ellipse are 1, 2, and 3 respectively. Region numbers are products of overlapping shapes. Which option is the most appropriate combination of P, Q, and R?
questions.s: P lies in the intersection of all three shapes (rectangle=1, triangle=2, ellipse=3), meaning P = 1 * 2 * 3 = 6 (or sum/product code). Q lies in triangle and ellipse only (2 * 3 = 6 or 2+3=5). R lies in rectangle and triangle (1 * 2 = 2 or matching association). Evaluating the options, (A) gives P = 6; Q = 5; R = 3.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q: A rectangle has length L and width W, where L > W. If the width W is increased by 10%, which one of the following statements is correct for all values of L and W?
o: Length of the diagonals increases by 10%.
questions.s: New width W' = 1.10 W. New Area A' = L * W' = L * (1.10 W) = 1.10 (LW) = 1.10 A. Area increases by exactly 10% regardless of the numerical values of L and W.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q:
Match statements by Shanthala (Column-I) with responses by Kanishk (Column-II):
P. This house is in a mess.
Q. I am not happy with the marks given to me.
R. Politics is a subject I avoid talking about.
S. I don't know what this word means.
with:
1. Alright, I won't bring it up during our conversations.
2. Well, you can easily look it up.
3. No problem, let me clear it up for you.
4. Don't worry, I will take it up with your teacher.
questions.s: P ('house is in a mess') pairs with 3 ('clear it up'). Q ('unhappy with marks') pairs with 4 ('take it up with teacher'). R ('politics is a subject I avoid') pairs with 1 ('won't bring it up'). S ('don't know what this word means') pairs with 2 ('look it up'). Hence P-3, Q-4, R-1, S-2.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q: Weight of a person as a function of age monotonically increases until 50 years and then monotonically decreases. Suppose this function is identical for two brothers with ages a1 and a2 (a1 < a2). Which statement is correct about their age on the day they attain the same weight?
questions.s: Since the function is strictly monotonic on [0, 50], it is one-to-one on that interval: two distinct ages < 50 cannot yield the same weight. Similarly, it is one-to-one for ages > 50. For f(a1) = f(a2) with a1 < a2, one brother must be on the rising branch (a1 < 50) and the other on the declining branch (a2 > 50). Thus a1 < 50 < a2.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q: A regular dodecagon (12-sided) is inscribed in a circle of radius r. All 12 isosceles triangles formed by connecting the center to the vertices are used to form squares of side r, using each triangle only once. The number of squares that can be formed and the number of triangles required to form each square are:
questions.s: Central angle of each triangle in dodecagon is 360°/12 = 30°. Area of one triangle = (1/2) * r * r * sin(30°) = (1/4) r^2. Total area of all 12 triangles = 12 * (1/4) r^2 = 3 r^2. Area of one square of side r is r^2. Therefore, exactly 3 r^2 / r^2 = 3 squares can be formed, requiring 12 / 3 = 4 triangles each.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q: If a real variable x satisfies 3^(x^2) = 27 * 9^x, then the value of 2^(x^2) / (2^x)^2 is:
questions.s: Rewrite equation with base 3: 3^(x^2) = 3^3 * (3^2)^x = 3^(2x + 3). Equating exponents: x^2 = 2x + 3 => x^2 - 2x = 3. Now evaluate the target expression: 2^(x^2) / (2^x)^2 = 2^(x^2) / 2^(2x) = 2^(x^2 - 2x). Substituting x^2 - 2x = 3 gives 2^3.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q: Number of patients per shift (X) consulting Dr. Gita in past 100 shifts: X=5 (20 shifts), X=6 (40 shifts), X=7 (30 shifts), X=8 (10 shifts). If amount earned is ₹ 1000(X - 0.2), what is the average amount earned per shift in the past 100 shifts?

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Suppose X and Y are random variables. The conditional expectation of X given Y is denoted by E[X|Y]. Then E[E[X|Y]] equals:
questions.s: By the Law of Total Expectation (Adam's Law / Tower Property), E[E[X|Y]] = E[X].

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: The number of additions and multiplications involved in performing Gaussian elimination on any n x n upper triangular matrix is of the order:
questions.s: An upper triangular system is already in row echelon form; no forward elimination is needed. Solving it requires only back-substitution: x_i = (b_i - sum_{j=i+1}^n a_ij x_j) / a_ii. Back-substitution requires sum_{i=1}^n (n - i) operations = n(n-1)/2, which is O(n^2).

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: The sum of the elements in each row of A in R^(nxn) is 1. If B = A^3 - 2A^2 + A, which one of the following statements is correct (for x in R^n)?
o: The equation Bx = 0 has no solution
The equation Bx = 0 has exactly two solutions
The equation Bx = 0 has infinitely many solutions
The equation Bx = 0 has a unique solution
questions.s: Since row sums of A equal 1, the all-ones vector 1 = [1, 1, ..., 1]^T is an eigenvector of A with eigenvalue λ = 1 (A 1 = 1). For polynomial B = A^3 - 2A^2 + A, the eigenvalue associated with 1 is g(1) = 1^3 - 2(1^2) + 1 = 0. Therefore B 1 = 0 1 = 0. Since B has eigenvalue 0, B is singular and det(B) = 0. A homogeneous system Bx = 0 with singular B always has non-trivial solutions, hence infinitely many solutions.

questions.subject: calc
questions.q: Let f(x) = (e^x - e^(-x)) / 2 for x in R. What is the value of f^(10)(0)?
questions.s: Notice f(x) = sinh(x). Derivatives alternate: f'(x) = cosh(x), f''(x) = sinh(x), ..., f^(2k)(x) = sinh(x), f^(2k-1)(x) = cosh(x). The 10th derivative is f^(10)(x) = sinh(x). Evaluated at x = 0: sinh(0) = (e^0 - e^0)/2 = 0.

questions.subject: ai
questions.q: Let p and q be propositions: S1: p -> q, S2: ¬p ∧ q, S3: ¬p ∨ q, S4: ¬p ∨ ¬q. Which option is correct?
questions.s: By definition of conditional implication, p -> q is logically equivalent to ¬p ∨ q. Hence S1 ≡ S3.

questions.subject: dbms
questions.q: If a relational decomposition is not dependency-preserving, which one of the following relational operators will be executed more frequently in order to maintain the dependencies?
questions.s: When a functional dependency X -> Y is not preserved in a decomposition, checking it requires joining the decomposed relations (natural join) upon every update/insert to reconstruct the original relation.

questions.subject: dbms
questions.q: Given Car(model, year, serial, color), Make(maker, model), Own(owner, serial): What does π_owner(Own ⨝ (σ_color='red'(Car ⨝ (σ_maker='ABC' Make)))) compute?
o: All owners of a red car, a car made by ABC, or a red car made by ABC
All owners of more than one car, where at least one car is red and made by ABC
All owners of a red car made by ABC
All red cars made by ABC
questions.s: σ_maker='ABC'(Make) selects models by ABC. Joining with Car and filtering σ_color='red' yields all serial numbers of red cars made by ABC. Joining with Own and projecting on owner yields all owners who own a red car made by ABC.

questions.subject: prog
questions.q: Hash table size 10 (indices 0..9) with h(x) = 3x mod 10 and linear probing. Keys inserted: 1, 4, 5, 6, 14, 15. The indices where 14 and 15 are stored are:
questions.s: Trace: 1 -> 3*1=3 (idx 3). 4 -> 3*4=12=2 (idx 2). 5 -> 3*5=15=5 (idx 5). 6 -> 3*6=18=8 (idx 8). 14 -> 3*14=42=2 (collides with 4 at idx 2, collides with 1 at idx 3, takes idx 4). 15 -> 3*15=45=5 (collides with 5 at idx 5, takes idx 6). Thus 14 and 15 are stored at 4 and 6.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Let continuous random variable X have CDF FX(x) = 0 for x <= t; (x - t)/(4 - t) for t <= x <= 4; 1 for x >= 4. If the median of X is 3, then what is the value of t?
questions.s: By definition, the median m satisfies FX(m) = 0.5. Since m = 3 lies in [t, 4]: (3 - t) / (4 - t) = 1/2 => 2(3 - t) = 4 - t => 6 - 2t = 4 - t => t = 2.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Let X = aZ + b, where Z ~ N(0, 1). Given E[X] = 1, E[(X - E[X])Z] = -2, E[(X - E[X])^2] = 4. The values of a, b are:
questions.s: E[X] = a E[Z] + b = a(0) + b = b = 1. X - E[X] = aZ. E[(X - E[X])Z] = E[(aZ)Z] = a E[Z^2] = a(1) = -2 => a = -2. Check variance: E[(aZ)^2] = a^2(1) = (-2)^2 = 4 (consistent). Thus a = -2, b = 1.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: It is given that P(X >= 2) = 0.25 for an exponentially distributed random variable X with E[X] = 1/λ. What is the value of λ?
questions.s: For X ~ Exp(λ), P(X >= x) = e^(-λx). Given P(X >= 2) = e^(-2λ) = 0.25 = 1/4. Taking natural logarithm: -2λ = ln(1/4) = -ln 4 = -2 ln 2 => 2λ = 2 ln 2 => λ = ln 2.

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: Linear classifier y = sign(w^T x + b). Parameters updated: w_new = w_old + y_n x_n, b_new = b_old + y_n whenever prediction != y_n. Consider (x_n, y_n = +1) with f(x_n; w_old, b_old) < 0. Then:
o: f(x_n; w_new, b_new) > f(x_n; w_old, b_old)
f(x_n; w_new, b_new) < f(x_n; w_old, b_old)
f(x_n; w_new, b_new) = f(x_n; w_old, b_old)
questions.s: f(x_n; w_new, b_new) = w_new^T x_n + b_new = (w_old + x_n)^T x_n + (b_old + 1) = w_old^T x_n + b_old + ||x_n||^2 + 1 = f(x_n; w_old, b_old) + (||x_n||^2 + 1). Since ||x_n||^2 + 1 > 0, the updated value is strictly greater.

questions.subject: prog
questions.q: A = [1, 2, 3], B = [4, 5, 6]. Which statement results in A = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]?
questions.s: In Python, `list.extend(iterable)` appends all elements of iterable to the list, giving [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]. `append(B)` would nest the list: [1, 2, 3, [4, 5, 6]].

questions.subject: calc
questions.q: Functions f: R -> R and g: R -> (1, ∞) are differentiable at c. Which of the following functions is/are ALWAYS differentiable at c?
questions.s: Linear combination (f ± g) and product (f · g) of differentiable functions at c are always differentiable at c. Quotient (f/g) is differentiable at c because g(c) > 1 != 0. Composition f ◦ g requires differentiability of f at g(c), which is not guaranteed.

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct?
o: R^n has a unique set of orthonormal basis vectors
R^n does not have a unique set of orthonormal basis vectors
Linearly independent vectors in R^n are orthonormal
Orthonormal vectors in R^n are linearly independent
questions.s: Any rotation or orthogonal transformation of the standard basis vectors yields another valid orthonormal basis for R^n, so it is not unique: (B). Orthonormal vectors are always mutually orthogonal and unit norm, which strictly implies linear independence: (D).

questions.subject: ai
questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct in a Bayesian network?
o: Variable elimination is an approximate inference algorithm
Gibbs sampling is an exact inference algorithm
Variable elimination is used to determine conditional probabilities
Rejection sampling is an approximate inference algorithm
questions.s: Variable elimination is an EXACT inference algorithm (not approximate), used to determine conditional probabilities: (C). Rejection sampling and Gibbs sampling are APPROXIMATE (stochastic sampling / MCMC) inference algorithms: (D).

questions.subject: prog
questions.q: For which of the following inputs does binary search take time O(log n) in the worst case?
o: An array of n integers in any order
A linked list of n integers in any order
An array of n integers in increasing order
A linked list of n integers in increasing order
questions.s: Binary search requires two properties to achieve O(log n) worst-case time: (1) sorted order, and (2) direct random access O(1) by index to find the middle element, which arrays provide but linked lists do not (traversing to middle in linked list takes O(n) time).

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: Let A = I_n + x x^T, where x in R^n, x^T x = 1. Which options is/are correct?
questions.s: Eigenvalues of x x^T are 1 (eigenvector x) and 0 (multiplicity n-1). Eigenvalues of A = I_n + x x^T are 1 + 1 = 2 (multiplicity 1) and 1 + 0 = 1 (multiplicity n-1). Since all eigenvalues are strictly positive (2 and 1), det(A) = 2 != 0, so A has full rank n (A) and A is invertible (B). Eigenvalues of A^(-1) are 1/2 and 1 (none negative).

questions.subject: prog
questions.q: Insertion sort is applied to [1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, x, 15, 13] and takes exactly two swaps to sort the array. Select all possible values of x.
questions.s: At the start, [1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11] is sorted. When x is processed: if 9 < x < 11 (e.g. x=10), x swaps with 11 (1 swap). Next, 15 is processed (0 swaps). Then 13 is processed: 13 swaps with 15 (1 swap). Total swaps = 1 + 1 = 2 swaps! If x=12, x takes 0 swaps, total=1 swap. If x=14, x takes 0 swaps, 13 takes 2 swaps (with 15 and 14) = 2 swaps (or check order). With x=10, exactly two swaps occur.

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: Let DIS-1(C1, C2) = max_{x in C1, y in C2} D(x, y) and DIS-2(C1, C2) = min_{x in C1, y in C2} D(x, y). Which statements is/are correct?
questions.s: By standard definition: Single linkage measures cluster distance by the minimum distance between any pair of points in the two clusters (DIS-2). Complete linkage measures cluster distance by the maximum distance between points in the two clusters (DIS-1).

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Three boxes: Box-1 has 2 black, 1 white; Box-2 has 1 black, 2 white; Box-3 has 3 black, 3 white. P(Box-1)=1/2, P(Box-2)=1/6, P(Box-3)=1/3. A ball is drawn at random and is white. Probability it came from Box-2 is ______ (rounded to two decimal places).

questions.subject: calc
questions.q: lim_{t -> +∞} (sqrt(t^2 + t) - t) = ______ (round off to one decimal place).
questions.s: Rationalize numerator: (sqrt(t^2 + t) - t)(sqrt(t^2 + t) + t) / (sqrt(t^2 + t) + t) = (t^2 + t - t^2) / (sqrt(t^2 + t) + t) = t / (t(sqrt(1 + 1/t) + 1)) = 1 / (sqrt(1 + 1/t) + 1). As t -> ∞, 1/t -> 0, yielding 1 / (1 + 1) = 1/2 = 0.5.

questions.subject: dbms
questions.q: Table Loan(loan_number, branch_name, amount) has: (L11, Banjara Hills, 90000), (L14, Kondapur, 50000), (L15, SR Nagar, 40000), (L22, SR Nagar, 25000), (L23, Balanagar, 80000), (L25, Kondapur, 70000), (L19, SR Nagar, 65000). Rows returned by: SELECT L1.loan_number FROM Loan L1 WHERE L1.amount > (SELECT MAX(L2.amount) FROM Loan L2 WHERE L2.branch_name = 'SR Nagar')?
questions.s: Subquery finds MAX(amount) for 'SR Nagar': values are 40000, 25000, 65000 -> MAX = 65000. Outer query selects loan_number with amount > 65000: L11 (90000), L23 (80000), L25 (70000). Total rows returned = 3.

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: Given data {(-1, 1), (2, -5), (3, 5)} of the form (x, y), we fit model y = wx using linear least-squares regression. The optimal value of w is ______ (rounded to three decimal places).
questions.s: For model y = wx without intercept, least-squares normal equation is w = (sum x_i y_i) / (sum x_i^2). sum x_i y_i = (-1)(1) + (2)(-5) + (3)(5) = -1 - 10 + 15 = 4. sum x_i^2 = (-1)^2 + 2^2 + 3^2 = 1 + 4 + 9 = 14. w = 4 / 14 = 2 / 7 ≈ 0.2857.

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: Naive Bayes for two classes y1, y2 with priors P(y1) = 1/3, P(y2) = 2/3. For feature vector x, P(x|y1) = 3/4 and P(x|y2) = 1/4. The probability of misclassifying x is ______ (rounded to two decimal places).
questions.s: Posterior numerator: for y1, P(y1)P(x|y1) = (1/3)(3/4) = 3/12. For y2, P(y2)P(x|y2) = (2/3)(1/4) = 2/12. Since 3/12 > 2/12, the Bayes classifier predicts y1. Misclassification occurs when true class is y2: P(error|x) = P(y2|x) = (2/12) / (3/12 + 2/12) = 2/5 = 0.40.

questions.subject: prob

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: Let A in R^(nxn) be such that A^3 = A. Which ONE statement is ALWAYS correct?
o: The sum of the diagonal elements of A is 1
A and A^2 have the same rank
questions.s: The minimal polynomial divides λ^3 - λ = λ(λ - 1)(λ + 1), which has distinct roots {0, 1, -1}. Hence A is diagonalizable. The non-zero eigenvalues of A are ±1, which square to 1 (non-zero). Thus the eigenspaces for non-zero eigenvalues of A and A^2 have the same dimension. Hence rank(A) = rank(A^2).

questions.q: 100 fair six-sided dice are thrown. Event A is that at least one of the dice shows a 1. Then P(A) =
questions.s: For a single die, probability of not showing 1 is 5/6. Since all 100 dice are independent, probability that none of the 100 dice shows 1 is (5/6)^100. Therefore, P(at least one 1) = 1 - P(none shows 1) = 1 - (5/6)^100.

questions.s: GROUP BY CUBE(D1, D2) produces all combinations of groupings: (D1, D2) has 3 * 2 = 6 tuples; (D1) has 3 tuples; (D2) has 2 tuples; () overall aggregate has 1 tuple. Total tuples = 6 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 12 (or (3 + 1) * (2 + 1) = 4 * 3 = 12).

Next, 'that' in B is True: C|A = {'other', 'this'}, A|B = {'this', 'that'}, B|C = {'that', 'other'}. Loop condition 'other' in C is still True. questions.subject: ml
questions.q: Which statements is/are correct about the rectified linear unit activation function ReLU(x) = max(x, 0) for x in R?
o: ReLU is not differentiable at x = 0
ReLU(x) = ReLU(ax), for all a in R
questions.s: ReLU(x) is continuous everywhere on R: (A). The left derivative at 0 is 0, while the right derivative at 0 is 1. Since left and right derivatives do not match at x = 0, it is not differentiable at x = 0: (C).

questions.subject: calc
questions.q: Consider f(x) = x^3 / 3 + 7x^2 / 2 + 10x + 133/2 on [-8, 0]. Which statements is/are correct?
o: The maximum value of f is attained at x = -5
The minimum value of f is attained at x = -2
The maximum value of f is 133/2
The minimum value of the derivative of f is attained at x = -7/2
questions.s: f'(x) = x^2 + 7x + 10 = (x + 2)(x + 5). Critical points: x = -5 (local max), x = -2 (local min). Boundary points: f(0) = 133/2 = 66.5; f(-5) = -125/3 + 175/2 - 50 + 66.5 = 62.33. Since f(0) = 66.5 > f(-5) = 62.33, global maximum is at x = 0 with value 133/2: (C). f'(x) is a parabola opening up with minimum at vertex x = -7/2: (D).

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: Let x1..x5 be orthonormal vectors in R^10. Consider matrix A = sum_{i=1}^5 x_i x_i^T. Which statements is/are correct?
o: Singular values of A are also its eigenvalues
Singular values of A are either 0 or 1
questions.s: A is symmetric positive semi-definite (A = A^T and x^T A x >= 0). For symmetric PSD matrices, singular values equal eigenvalues: (A). A is an orthogonal projection onto the 5D subspace spanned by {x1..x5}, so its eigenvalues are 1 (multiplicity 5) and 0 (multiplicity 5). Thus singular values are either 0 or 1: (B). Since rank is 5 < 10, det(A) = 0 and A is not invertible.

questions.subject: calc
questions.q: Let f: R -> R be twice-differentiable with f''(x) > 0 for all x in R. Which statements is/are ALWAYS correct?
o: There does not exist x and y, x != y, such that f'(x) = f'(y) = 0
f has at most one global minimum
f has at most one local minimum
questions.s: f''(x) > 0 implies f'(x) is strictly increasing. By Rolle's theorem / injectivity of f', f'(x) = 0 can have at most one solution. Hence f has at most one stationary point, meaning at most one local minimum (D) and at most one global minimum (C). Furthermore, f'(x) = f'(y) = 0 for x != y is impossible: (B). (A is not guaranteed, e.g. f(x) = e^x has f''(x)>0 but no minimum).

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: An n x n real matrix A satisfies ||Ax||^2 = ||x||^2 for all x in R^n (Euclidean norm). Which statements is/are ALWAYS correct?
o: A = I is the only solution
The eigenvalues of A are either +1 or -1
questions.s: ||Ax||^2 = x^T A^T A x = x^T x for all x implies A^T A = I_n by polarization identity. Thus A is an orthogonal matrix: (A). Since det(A) = ±1 != 0, A is non-singular and has full rank n: (D). (B is false as -I or any rotation is orthogonal. C is false because real orthogonal matrices can have complex eigenvalues e^(iθ)).

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: Hard-margin SVM f(x) = sign(w^T x + b) trained on Class-1: {[2,0]^T, [0,2]^T, [2,2]^T} and Class-2: {[0,0]^T}. Which options is/are correct?
o: The number of support vectors is 3
questions.s: The closest points between the two classes are Class-2 origin (0,0) and Class-1 points (2,0) and (0,2). The midpoint of the closest segments is at (1,0) and (0,1), forming the line x1 + x2 = 2. Normal vector w = [1, 1]^T, separating hyperplane x1 + x2 - 1 = 0 with margin γ = 1/||w|| = 1/√2, or canonical margin between parallel hyperplanes is √2. The support vectors are (0,0), (2,0), (0,2) — exactly 3 support vectors.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: X_i in {0, 1} with P(X_i = 1) = p, independent. Let p_hat = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n X_i. Which statements is/are correct?
o: As n increases, variance of p_hat decreases
Variance of p_hat does not depend on n
questions.s: E[p_hat] = (1/n) * n * p = p (unbiased estimator): (A). Var(p_hat) = Var(sum X_i) / n^2 = (n * p(1-p)) / n^2 = p(1-p)/n. As sample size n increases, the variance p(1-p)/n strictly decreases: (C).

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: Two classes in R^d with means μ_red and μ_green. Classifier calculates f(x) = ||μ_red - x||^2 - ||μ_green - x||^2 and assigns red if f(x) < 0, else green. Which statements is/are correct?
o: Sample x = 0 is assigned green if ||μ_red|| < ||μ_green||
f is a linear function of x
f(x) = w^T x + b, where w and b are functions of μ_red and μ_green
f is a quadratic polynomial in x
questions.s: Expanding the squared Euclidean norms: f(x) = (||μ_red||^2 - 2 μ_red^T x + ||x||^2) - (||μ_green||^2 - 2 μ_green^T x + ||x||^2) = 2(μ_green - μ_red)^T x + (||μ_red||^2 - ||μ_green||^2). The quadratic ||x||^2 terms cancel out completely! Thus f(x) is an affine / linear function of x (w^T x + b with w = 2(μ_green - μ_red)). (B) and (C) are correct.

questions.subject: dbms
questions.q: Person(aadhaar CHAR(12) PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(32)); Customer(name VARCHAR(32), email VARCHAR(32) PRIMARY KEY, phone CHAR(10), aadhaar CHAR(12), FOREIGN KEY (aadhaar) REFERENCES Person(aadhaar)). Which statements is/are correct?
o: aadhaar is a candidate key in the Customer relation
phone can be NULL in the Customer relation
aadhaar is a candidate key in the Person relation
aadhaar can be NULL in the Person relation
questions.s: In Person, aadhaar is declared PRIMARY KEY, so it is a candidate key: (C). In Customer, phone is not constrained by NOT NULL or PRIMARY KEY, so it can be NULL: (B). In Customer, aadhaar is a foreign key (a customer may share aadhaar or not have one unless NOT NULL, not necessarily unique): (A is false). Primary keys can never be NULL: (D is false).

questions.subject: dbms
questions.q: Relation R(ABCDEFG) with FDs: A -> BCEF, E -> DG, BC -> A. Which statements is/are correct?
o: A is the only candidate key of R
A, BC are the candidate keys of R
A, BC, E are the candidate keys of R
Relation R is not in Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF)
questions.s: Compute closures: A+ = {A,B,C,E,F,D,G} = R => A is a candidate key. (BC)+ = {A,B,C,E,F,D,G} = R => BC is a candidate key. E+ = {E,D,G} != R => E is not a key. Candidate keys are A and BC: (B). For BCNF, every determinant must be a superkey. In E -> DG, E is not a superkey, so R is NOT in BCNF: (D).

questions.subject: prog
questions.q: In an unweighted undirected graph G with vertices {a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h}: shortest path between a and d is a-b-c-d (length 3); between e and h is e-f-g-h (length 3); between a and h is a-f-c-h (length 3). Which of the following is/are NOT edges of G?
questions.s: If (b, d) were an edge, path a-b-d would have length 2, contradicting shortest path a-b-c-d (length 3). If (e, g) were an edge, path e-g-h would have length 2, contradicting shortest path e-f-g-h (length 3). Similarly, (b, h) would create a shorter path. Hence (b, d), (b, h), (e, g) cannot be edges of G.

questions.subject: calc
questions.q: Let f: R -> R be such that |f(x) - f(y)| <= (x - y)^2 for all x, y in R. Then f(1) - f(0) = ______ (Answer in integer).
questions.s: For any x and y with x != y, divide by |x - y|: |(f(x) - f(y)) / (x - y)| <= |x - y|. Taking the limit as y -> x: |f'(x)| <= lim_{y -> x} |x - y| = 0. Since |f'(x)| <= 0, f'(x) = 0 for all x in R. A function whose derivative is zero everywhere on R is a constant function f(x) = c. Therefore f(1) - f(0) = c - c = 0.

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: Dataset D has zero mean sum x^(i) = 0. Covariance matrix has eigenvalues λ_i = 100^(2-i) for 1 <= i <= 100. Let u in R^100 be the direction of maximum variance with u^T u = 1. The value of (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n (u^T x^(i))^2 is:
questions.s: Sample variance along unit direction u is u^T Σ u. The direction of maximum variance is the principal eigenvector of Σ corresponding to the largest eigenvalue λ_1. Here λ_i = 100^(2-i). For i = 1, λ_1 = 100^(2-1) = 100^1 = 100. Thus max variance = u^T Σ u = 100.

questions.q: A bag contains 5 white and 10 black balls. n balls are drawn one at a time with replacement. S_n denotes total black balls drawn. The expectation of S_100 is ______ (round to one decimal place).
questions.s: Drawing with replacement means each trial is independent with success (black ball) probability p = 10 / (5 + 10) = 10/15 = 2/3. For n = 100 draws, S_100 follows Binomial(n=100, p=2/3). E[S_100] = n * p = 100 * (2/3) = 200/3 ≈ 66.67.

questions.subject: ga
questions.q: Five integers are picked from 0 to 20, with possible repetitions, such that their mean is 12, median is 18, and they have a single mode of 20. Ignoring permutations, the number of ways to pick these five integers is:
questions.s: Let sorted integers be x1 <= x2 <= x3 <= x4 <= x5. Mean = 12 => sum = 60. Median x3 = 18. Mode is unique and equals 20, so 20 must appear at least twice: x4 = 20, x5 = 20. Then x1 + x2 + 18 + 20 + 20 = 60 => x1 + x2 = 2. Since 0 <= x1 <= x2: possible pairs are (0, 2) and (1, 1). If {1, 1, 18, 20, 20}, both 1 and 20 appear twice, resulting in a bimodal distribution (contradicting 'single mode'). Hence only {0, 2, 18, 20, 20} is valid, giving exactly 1 way.

questions.q:
Rishi and Swathi are students of Class 5. Pavan and Tanvi are students of Class 4. Rishi and Pavan are boys. Swathi and Tanvi are girls. The four students played a total of three games of chess one after another. A player who lost a game did not participate in any more games. It was observed that:
(i) the first game was the only game where two students of the same class played against each other,
(ii) the students of Class 5 won more games than the students of Class 4, and
(iii) the boys won two games and the girls won one game.
The student who did not lose any game is:
questions.s: In a 3-game elimination, the undefeated player wins Game 2 and Game 3. Condition (ii) means Class 5 won 2 games and Class 4 won 1 game. Condition (iii) means boys won 2 games and girls won 1 game. Since the champion won 2 games, both wins belong to the same person. Thus the champion must be a boy from Class 5, which uniquely identifies Rishi.

questions.q: P, Q, R, S, X, and Y are distinct single-digit whole numbers taking values from 0 to 9. PQ is a two-digit number with Q in the units place and P in the tens place. Similarly, RS is a two-digit number. It is known that PQ and RS are consecutive numbers and (PQ)^2 + (RS)^2 = XYP, with XYP being a three-digit number. The value of Y is:
questions.s: Testing consecutive two-digit integers: 19^2 + 20^2 = 361 + 400 = 761. Here PQ = 19 (P=1, Q=9), RS = 20 (R=2, S=0), and XYP = 761 (X=7, Y=6, P=1). The digits {1, 9, 2, 0, 7, 6} are all distinct whole numbers from 0 to 9. Therefore, Y = 6.

questions.q: In a circle of radius 10 cm with center O, points P, Q, and R lie on the circle such that PQ = RQ and angle PQR = 45 deg. The area of the shaded region PQRO is:

In triangle OPQ, OP = OQ = 10 and the angle POQ = 135 deg. Area(OPQ) = (1/2) * 10 * 10 * sin(135 deg) = 50 * (1/sqrt(2)) = 25*sqrt(2). By symmetry, Area(OQR) = 25*sqrt(2). questions.subject: prog
questions.q: Consider that the quick sort algorithm is used to sort an array of n distinct randomly ordered elements. In every call, the pivot is chosen as the first element of the current subarray. Let T(n) denote the expected time to sort the array. Assume that the time to partition is linear in the size of the current subarray. Which recurrence correctly represents T(n)?
questions.s: With random ordering, the rank of the first element is equally likely to be any integer k in {0, 1, ..., n-1} with probability 1/n. Partitioning leaves subarrays of sizes k and n - k - 1. Taking the expectation yields T(n) = (1/n) sum_{k=0}^{n-1} [T(k) + T(n - k - 1)] + O(n).

AD and ED are the only candidate keys of R.
A, E and CD are the only candidate keys of R.
A and CD are the only candidate keys of R.
questions.s: Attribute D does not appear on the right side of any functional dependency, so D must be present in every candidate key. Computing attribute closures: (AD)+ = {A, D, B, C, E} = R; (ED)+ = {E, D, A, B, C} = R; (CD)+ = {C, D, E, A, B} = R. None of their proper subsets contains D and determines R. Hence AD, ED, and CD are the only candidate keys.

questions.q: Consider that the visualization of a 3-dimensional data cube is showing Sales Quantity for each combination of the attributes Product Type, Month and Country. From this, if we want to further visualize the Sales Quantity for each combination of Product Type, Month and State, which OLAP operation should be performed?
questions.s: State is a lower (more granular) level of aggregation within the geographic concept hierarchy (Country -> State -> City). Moving from a higher-level summary (Country) to a more detailed level (State) is the Drill-down operation.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Let M be a randomly chosen non-empty subset of S = {1, 2, 3, ..., 2026}. Which of the following is the probability that the product of all the elements of M is even?
questions.s: S contains 1013 odd numbers and 1013 even numbers. Total non-empty subsets = 2^2026 - 1. The product of elements is odd if and only if all chosen elements are odd; the number of such non-empty subsets is 2^1013 - 1. Thus subsets with even product = (2^2026 - 1) - (2^1013 - 1) = 2^2026 - 2^1013 = 2^1013(2^1013 - 1). Probability = 2^1013(2^1013 - 1) / (2^2026 - 1).

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Suppose that a computer program provides a non-negative and integer-valued random solution to the equation n1 + n2 + n3 + n4 = 20. Which of the following is the probability that all of n1, n2, n3, n4 in the provided solution are positive?
questions.s: By stars-and-bars, total non-negative integer solutions to n1 + n2 + n3 + n4 = 20 is C(20 + 4 - 1, 4 - 1) = C(23, 3). For strictly positive integer solutions (ni >= 1), substitute ni = yi + 1 with yi >= 0, giving y1 + y2 + y3 + y4 = 16, which has C(16 + 4 - 1, 4 - 1) = C(19, 3) solutions. Probability = C(19, 3) / C(23, 3).

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: Let M = [[cos theta, -sin theta], [sin theta, cos theta]] be a 2x2 matrix, where theta = 2*pi/5, and I2 is the 2x2 identity matrix. Which of the following options is equal to M^2026?
questions.s: M represents a 2D counter-clockwise rotation by angle theta. M^k represents rotation by k*theta. For theta = 2*pi/5, M^5 is rotation by 2*pi, so M^5 = I2. 2026 = 5 * 405 + 1, so M^2026 = (M^5)^405 * M^1 = I2 * M = M.

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: Consider a set S1 = {x = (x1, x2, x3)^T in R^3 | x^T x <= 16}. Let S2 be another set which is a subspace of R^3 with dimension two. Which of the following gives the area of S1 intersect S2?
questions.s: S1 is a closed solid sphere of radius r = sqrt(16) = 4 centered at the origin. S2 is a 2D subspace, which geometrically is a plane passing through the origin. The intersection of a sphere centered at the origin with a plane passing through the origin is a circular disk of the exact same radius r = 4. Area = pi * r^2 = pi * 4^2 = 16*pi.

questions.subject: ai
questions.q: Sentence X is said to entail Sentence Y if whenever X is TRUE, Y also must hold TRUE. Which of the following statements is/are correct if X entails Y?
o: X and not Y is FALSE
questions.s: By definition of semantic entailment (X |= Y): whenever X is true, Y is true. Thus the implication X => Y is valid (always true), which means X and not Y is unsatisfiable (FALSE). In natural language, this translates to 'if X then Y'. 'if Y then X' denotes the converse, which is not guaranteed.

questions.subject: prog
questions.q:
You are given the following Pre-order and In-order traversals of a Binary Tree T with nodes E, F, G, P, Q, R, S:
Pre-order: P Q S E R F G
In-order: S Q E P F R G
Which of the following statements is/are true about the Binary Tree T?
o: Node P is the root of T
The Post-order traversal of T is: S E Q F G R P
Node Q has only one child
The left subtree of node R contains the node G
questions.s: Root is P (first in pre-order). In-order partitions: Left subtree {S, Q, E}, Right subtree {F, R, G}. For left subtree: pre-order Q S E, in-order S Q E -> Q is root, S is left child, E is right child (Q has two children, so (C) is false). For right subtree: pre-order R F G, in-order F R G -> R is root, F is left child, G is right child (G is in right subtree, so (D) is false). Post-order traversal visits left-right-root: S E Q F G R P. Statements (A) and (B) are true.

questions.subject: dbms
questions.q: Consider two relations r and s defined on the relational schemas R(A,B) and S(E,C), respectively. A is the primary key of R and E is a foreign key of S referencing A in R. Which of the following operations will NEVER violate the foreign key constraint?
questions.s: Inserting into the referenced relation r only adds potential target keys, which cannot violate referential integrity. Deleting from the referencing relation s removes child references, which also cannot violate foreign key constraints. In contrast, deleting from r or inserting into s can create dangling references.

questions.subject: calc
questions.q: Let f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2 be a function defined on (-1, 3]. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
o: f(x) has exactly two roots in [-0.9, 0].
f(x) has a minimum at 2 only.
questions.s: f'(x) = 3x^2 - 6x = 3x(x - 2) = 0 => critical points at x = 0 and x = 2. f''(0) = -6 < 0 (local maximum at 0 with f(0)=2); f''(2) = 6 > 0 (local minimum at 2 with f(2)=-2). f(1) = 1 - 3 + 2 = 0, so 1 is a root. In [-0.9, 0], f'(x) > 0 so f is strictly increasing; f(-0.9) < 0 and f(0) = 2 > 0 implies exactly ONE root, not two.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Suppose a random variable Z follows Normal(mu = 0, sigma^2 = 1) with pdf g(z) and cdf G(z). Another random variable Y follows t1 distribution (standard Cauchy) with pdf h(y) and cdf H(y). Let c be the positive real number for which g(c) = h(c). Which of the following statements is/are correct?
questions.s: Both distributions are symmetric about 0, so G(0) = H(0) = 0.5. At 0, g(0) = 1/sqrt(2*pi) ~= 0.3989 while h(0) = 1/pi ~= 0.3183, so g(0) != h(0). For 0 < x < c, g(x) > h(x), so G(c) > H(c). By symmetry G(-c) = 1 - G(c) < 1 - H(c) = H(-c). Statements (A) and (C) are correct.

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: Consider that for a supervised learning task, the objective function being minimized is fw(x) = wx, where x in R is the input and w in R is the parameter. Stochastic Gradient Descent with learning rate of 0.10 is used for parameter updates. Suppose that at the end of iteration i, the value of w becomes 10.00. Let x = 10.00 be the input for iteration (i + 1). The value of w at the end of iteration (i + 1) is: (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.s: The gradient of fw(x) with respect to w is d(wx)/dw = x. The SGD update rule is w_{i+1} = w_i - eta * x. Given w_i = 10.00, eta = 0.10, and x = 10.00: w_{i+1} = 10.00 - 0.10 * 10.00 = 10.00 - 1.00 = 9.00.

questions.subject: ai
questions.q: Consider the game tree for a two-player turn-taking minimax game. MAX starts at root with strategies 1, 2, 3. MIN then plays with strategies 1, 2, 3. Terminal utilities: under branch 1: (8, 6, -1); under branch 2: (1, 5, 7); under branch 3: (-4, -3, -12). Both players choose optimal strategies. At the root, the best strategy for MAX is: (Answer in integer)
questions.s: MIN minimizes utility: Branch 1 evaluates to min(8, 6, -1) = -1. Branch 2 evaluates to min(1, 5, 7) = 1. Branch 3 evaluates to min(-4, -3, -12) = -12. MAX chooses the branch maximizing value: max(-1, 1, -12) = 1, which corresponds to strategy 2.

questions.subject: prog
questions.q: Let A be a sorted array containing 1000 distinct integers. You perform a recursive binary search on A to find an element y. Suppose each comparison checks whether the middle element computed during the current recursive step is equal to, less than, or greater than y. The maximum number of comparisons that may have to be performed if y is not an element of A is: (Answer in integer)
questions.s: The maximum recursion depth for binary search on an array of size n = 1000 is ceil(log2(n + 1)) = ceil(log2(1001)) = 10. An unsuccessful search reaches the deepest leaf of the decision tree, requiring exactly 10 comparisons.

questions.subject: dbms
questions.q: In a relational database, a B+ Tree Index is constructed on a key field. Node size = 4096 bytes, Node Pointer size = 10 bytes, Search Key Field size = 11 bytes and Data Record Pointer size = 12 bytes. The maximum number of Node Pointers that can be present in a non-leaf node of the B+ Tree is: (Answer in integer)
questions.s: In a non-leaf node of order p, there are p node pointers and (p - 1) search keys. Data record pointers are only stored in leaf nodes. The constraint is: p * 10 + (p - 1) * 11 <= 4096 => 21p - 11 <= 4096 => 21p <= 4107 => p <= 195.57. Hence maximum node pointers = 195.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: The number of bijections f(.) from the set S = {1, 2, 3, 4} to itself such that f(f(n)) = n for all n in S, is: (Answer in integer)
questions.s: A bijection with f(f(n)) = n is an involution (permutation whose square is identity). Its cycle decomposition contains only 1-cycles (fixed points) and 2-cycles (transpositions): (1) 0 transpositions: 1 way. (2) 1 transposition: C(4, 2) = 6 ways. (3) 2 disjoint transpositions: 4! / (2! * 2! * 2!) = 3 ways. Total = 1 + 6 + 3 = 10.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Let X be an exponentially distributed random variable with mean lambda (> 0). If P(X > 5) = 0.35, then the conditional probability P(X > 10 | X > 5) is: (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.s: By the memoryless property of the exponential distribution, P(X > s + t | X > t) = P(X > s) for all s, t >= 0. Here t = 5 and s = 5, so P(X > 10 | X > 5) = P(X > 5) = 0.35.

questions.subject: calc
questions.q: The value of sum_{i=0}^infinity sum_{j=1}^infinity 2^(-i) * 3^(-j) is: (Answer in integer)
questions.s: The double sum separates into product of two geometric series: (sum_{i=0}^infinity (1/2)^i) * (sum_{j=1}^infinity (1/3)^j). The first series = 1 / (1 - 1/2) = 2. The second series = (1/3) / (1 - 1/3) = (1/3) / (2/3) = 1/2. Product = 2 * (1/2) = 1.
