questions.q: Which of the following statements is true for Ridge Regression?
o: The regularizer in the objective function of Ridge Regression is used to guard against scenarios where the model works well for the test data, but poorly for the training data.
The regularizer of Ridge Regression uses L1 norm.
Ridge Regression aims to reduce the number of parameters that have negative values.
The regularizer of Ridge Regression may increase the bias of the model, but it helps in reducing the variance in predictions.
questions.s: Ridge regression introduces an L2 penalty on the weights (lambda * ||w||_2^2). By shrinking coefficient magnitudes towards zero, it trades off a slight increase in model bias for a substantial decrease in variance, preventing overfitting and mitigating multicollinearity.

questions.subject: ai
questions.q:
Assume that a Creative (C) person will Succeed (S) if the person is also Disciplined (D), but will not succeed otherwise. Now, consider the following statements:
(i) C and S <=> D
(ii) C => (S <=> D)
(iii) C <=> ((D => S) or not S)
Which of the following options is correct?
questions.s: Given premise: For a creative person (C is True), they succeed if and only if they are disciplined, so S <=> D. When C is False, success is unspecified or not tied to D. Thus C => (S <=> D) accurately captures the conditional behavior. Statement (i) falsely restricts D when C is False. Hence only (ii) is TRUE.

questions.subject: prog
prog
questions.q: Consider a directed graph G = (V, E) without self-loops. Let G^R be the graph obtained by reversing the directions of all edges in G. Which of the following statements must always be true, regardless of the structure of G?
o: If u is a reachable vertex in the BFS of G^R from v, then u is also a reachable vertex in the DFS of G from v.
In G^R, the BFS traversal from v will visit exactly the same set of vertices as the DFS from v in G.
The order of vertices visited in the BFS of G^R from v is the reverse of the order of vertices visited in the DFS of G from v.
If u is a reachable vertex in the DFS of G from v, then v is also a reachable vertex in the BFS of G^R from u.
questions.s: If u is reachable from v in G, there exists a directed path v = w0 -> w1 -> ... -> wk = u in G. In G^R, every edge is reversed, so wk -> ... -> w1 -> w0 is a valid directed path from u to v in G^R. BFS from u in G^R explores all reachable vertices, so it will always visit v.

questions.subject: dbms
questions.q: Consider a B+ Tree where max keys per leaf is 2 and max pointers per non-leaf is 3. Root contains keys [5, 8] with leaves [1, 5], [7, 8], [9, 12]. Which option denotes the key value(s) stored in the root node after inserting key 3?
questions.s: Inserting 3 into leaf [1, 5] causes overflow ([1, 3, 5]). Leaf splits into [1, 3] and [5], pushing 3 to the parent. The root already contains [5, 8], so adding 3 makes it [3, 5, 8] (overflow, max keys is 2). The root splits: middle key 5 is pushed up to become the new single-key root [5].

questions.subject: dbms
questions.q: Consider relations X(P,Q,R), Y(P,Q,S) and Z(P,T). Expression: Pi_{P,R,S}[(sigma_{Q='Q3' or R='R2'}[X |><| Y]) |><| (sigma_{S > 1}[Y |><| Z])]. Which option is the correct output?
o: Three rows (P1, R1, 2), (P1, R1, 5) and (P2, R2, 6)
questions.s: From Y |><| Z: Z contains P1, P3, P4. P2 is not in Z, so P2 is eliminated from (sigma_{S > 1}[Y |><| Z]). For P1: Y has (P1, Q1, 2) and (P1, Q2, 5), both S > 1. In X |><| Y, condition Q='Q3' or R='R2' matches P3 (Q3) and P2/P3 (R2), but the subsequent natural join on (P, Q, S) filters to consistent P-tuples. Evaluating across the relations yields exactly two rows: (P1, R1, 2) and (P1, R1, 5).

questions.subject: dbms
questions.q: Consider three concept hierarchies: Time (Year -> Month -> Day), Location (Country -> State -> City), and Item (Category -> Type -> Item). Which option denotes the total number of possible data cuboids?
questions.s: Each dimension hierarchy has 3 explicit levels plus the top 'ALL' level, giving 3 + 1 = 4 levels per dimension. In a lattice of cuboids, a cuboid corresponds to selecting one level from each dimension independently. Total cuboids = 4 * 4 * 4 = 4^3 = 64.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Let X and Y be two independent random variables. X follows Bernoulli(p = 0.3) and Y follows Normal(mu = 0, sigma^2 = 100). Which of the following options is the variance of (2X - 1)Y?
questions.s: Notice that for any Bernoulli variable X in {0, 1}, the expression 2X - 1 takes values in {-1, +1}. Therefore (2X - 1)^2 = 1 with probability 1! Because X and Y are independent: Var((2X - 1)Y) = E[((2X - 1)Y)^2] - (E[(2X - 1)Y])^2 = E[(2X - 1)^2] * E[Y^2] - (E[2X - 1] * E[Y])^2 = 1 * 100 - 0 = 100.

questions.subject: calc
questions.q: Evaluate L = lim_{n -> infinity} sum_{k=0}^n (e^(-n) * n^k) / k!. Which of the following is the value of L?
questions.s: The term sum_{k=0}^n (e^(-n) * n^k) / k! equals P(Kn <= n) where Kn ~ Poisson(n). Mean of Kn is n and variance is n. By the Central Limit Theorem, (Kn - n)/sqrt(n) converges in distribution to standard normal N(0, 1). Thus lim_{n -> infinity} P(Kn <= n) = lim P((Kn - n)/sqrt(n) <= 0) = Phi(0) = 0.5.

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: Let gamma1, gamma2, gamma3 be the eigenvalues of the matrix [[1, 0, 0], [0, cos t, sin t], [0, -sin t, cos t]], where t in [-pi, pi]. Which option lists all possible values of t satisfying gamma1 + gamma2 + gamma3 = 1 + sqrt(2)?
questions.s: The sum of the eigenvalues of any matrix equals its trace. Trace = 1 + cos t + cos t = 1 + 2 cos t. Equating to 1 + sqrt(2): 1 + 2 cos t = 1 + sqrt(2) => cos t = sqrt(2)/2 = 1/sqrt(2). For t in [-pi, pi], the solutions are t = pi/4 and t = -pi/4.

questions.subject: ml
questions.q: 20 stories of Author X and 10 stories of Author Y were classified. Out of X's stories, 6 were classified as Y (14 classified as X). Out of Y's stories, 2 were classified as X (8 classified as Y). Which statements are true?
o: Precision of Class X is higher than the Precision of Class Y.
Recall of Class X is higher than the Recall of Class Y.
questions.s: Total stories = 30. Correct predictions = 14 + 8 = 22. Accuracy = 22/30 = 11/15. Precision(X) = 14 / (14 + 2) = 14/16 = 0.875. Precision(Y) = 8 / (8 + 6) = 8/14 = 0.571, so Precision(X) > Precision(Y). Recall(X) = 14/20 = 0.70 while Recall(Y) = 8/10 = 0.80, so Recall(X) < Recall(Y). Statements (A) and (B) are true.

questions.subject: ai
questions.q: Let P(x) be a predicate. Which of the following statements is/are NOT valid in first-order logic?
o: forall x P(x) => exists x P(x)
exists x P(x) => forall x P(x)
exists x P(x) <=> forall x P(x)
forall x P(x) => exists x not P(x)
questions.s: In FOL with non-empty domains, 'forall x P(x) => exists x P(x)' is valid. However, existence does not imply universality (exists x P(x) does not imply forall x P(x)), so (B) and (C) are invalid. 'forall x P(x) => exists x not P(x)' is self-contradictory and invalid. Hence (B), (C), and (D) are NOT valid.

questions.subject: prog
questions.q: Consider sorting array P = [1, 2, 3, 5, 4] using Bubble Sort (N1 comparisons) and Insertion Sort (N2 comparisons). Which of the following options is/are correct?
o: IS on P will perform only one swap
Both BS and IS on P will make at least one unnecessary comparison (i.e., comparing elements that are already in correct order)
questions.s: Standard Bubble Sort performs n(n-1)/2 = 10 comparisons. Insertion Sort inserts 1 (0), 2 (1), 3 (1), 5 (1), and 4 (2 comparisons: 4 < 5, 4 > 3), giving N2 = 5 comparisons. Thus N1 > N2. Only elements 5 and 4 are swapped once in IS. Both algorithms compare already-sorted elements (e.g., 1 with 2, 2 with 3). Statements (B), (C), (D) are correct.

questions.subject: prog
questions.q:
Consider the given Python program:
def outer():
    x = []
    def inner(val):
        x.append(val)
        return x
    return inner
f1 = outer()
f2 = outer()
print(f1(10)) # Line P
print(f1(20)) # Line Q
print(f2(30)) # Line R
print(f1(40)) # Line S
Which of the following options is/are correct?
o: f1 and f2 share the same list x
questions.s: Each invocation of outer() creates a distinct closure with its own fresh list x. f1 maintains its own list: f1(10) -> [10], f1(20) -> [10, 20], f1(40) -> [10, 20, 40]. f2 maintains a separate list: f2(30) -> [30]. Therefore, statements (B) and (D) are correct.

questions.subject: dbms
questions.q: Given Employee(EmpID, TeamID), display EmpID and the size of their team (TeamSize). Which SQL query correctly produces this result?
o: SELECT E.EmpID, B.TeamSize FROM Employee AS E, (SELECT TeamID, COUNT(TeamID) AS TeamSize FROM Employee GROUP BY TeamID) AS B WHERE E.TeamID = B.TeamID
SELECT A.EmpID, COUNT(B.TeamID) AS TeamSize FROM Employee AS A, Employee AS B WHERE A.TeamID = B.TeamID AND A.EmpID = B.EmpID GROUP BY A.EmpID
SELECT B.EmpID, B.TeamSize FROM (SELECT EmpID, COUNT(TeamID) AS TeamSize FROM Employee GROUP BY EmpID) AS B
SELECT A.EmpID, B.TeamSize FROM Employee AS A, (SELECT COUNT(TeamID) AS TeamSize FROM Employee GROUP BY TeamID) AS B WHERE A.TeamID = B.TeamID
questions.s: Query (A) pre-aggregates team counts by grouping by TeamID in derived table B, and joins it back to the original Employee table on TeamID, correctly outputting each employee's ID alongside their team's total size.

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: Let M = (In - (1/n) * 1 1^T) where 1 = (1, 1, ..., 1)^T in R^n and In is identity. Which of the following options is/are correct?
questions.s: M is the centering matrix. (1) M is symmetric: M^T = M. (2) M is idempotent: M^2 = M (it projects onto the orthogonal complement of the all-ones vector), so M is an orthogonal projection matrix. Trace(M) = Trace(In) - (1/n)Trace(1 1^T) = n - (1/n)(n) = n - 1 != n. Statements (A) and (D) are correct.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Let X1, ..., Xn be n independent N(0, 1) random variables. Let X_bar = (1/n) sum X_i. Which statements are correct?
o: sum_{i=1}^n X_i^2 follows Chi-square distribution with n degrees of freedom.
sum_{i=1}^n (X_i - X_bar)^2 follows Chi-square distribution with (n - 1) degrees of freedom.
X1^2 + Xn^2 follows exponential distribution with mean 2.
(sqrt(n) * X_bar)^2 follows Chi-square distribution with 2 degrees of freedom.
questions.s: Sum of squares of n standard normals is Chi-square(n). By Cochran's theorem, sum (X_i - X_bar)^2 is Chi-square(n-1). X1^2 + Xn^2 is Chi-square(2), which is identical to an Exponential distribution with parameter lambda = 1/2 and mean 1/lambda = 2. (sqrt(n) * X_bar)^2 is Chi-square with 1 degree of freedom, not 2.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Let X be a discrete valued random variable with cumulative distribution function F(x). Which of the following statements is/are correct?
o: F(x) is always a positive function.
F(x) is a left continuous function.
questions.s: Every CDF is non-decreasing: x1 <= x2 => F(x1) <= F(x2). For a discrete random variable, F(x) is a step function with jump discontinuities at each point in the support where P(X = x) > 0. By convention, CDFs are right-continuous, not left-continuous, and F(x) can be 0 for values below the support.

R12 is a many-to-many relationship between E1 and E2 with total participation. The minimum number of relations required to convert the ER model into relational 3NF is: (Answer in integer)
questions.s: Converting into 3NF: (1) Entity E1 table: E1(A11, A12, A13). (2) Entity E2 base table: E2(A21, A23). (3) Separate relation for multivalued attribute A22: E2_A22(A21, A22). (4) Separate relation for many-to-many relationship R12: R12(A11, A21). Total relations = 4.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: For a dataset {x1, ..., xn} with n = 100: (1/2000) * sum_{i=1}^n sum_{j=1}^n (xi - xj)^2 = 99. Let x_bar = (1/n) sum xi. The value of (1/99) * sum_{i=1}^n (xi - x_bar)^2 is: (Answer in integer)
questions.s: Standard statistical identity: sum_{i=1}^n sum_{j=1}^n (xi - xj)^2 = 2n * sum_{i=1}^n (xi - x_bar)^2. For n = 100, 2n = 200. Thus: (1/2000) * 200 * sum (xi - x_bar)^2 = (1/10) * sum (xi - x_bar)^2 = 99, which gives sum (xi - x_bar)^2 = 990. Hence (1/99) * sum_{i=1}^n (xi - x_bar)^2 = 990 / 99 = 10.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Let X ~ Uniform(-1, 1). The conditional distribution of Y given X = x is Uniform(x^2 - 0.1, x^2 + 0.1). The value of correlation(X, Y) is: (Answer in integer)
questions.s: E[X] = 0 by symmetry of Uniform(-1, 1). E[Y|X=x] = x^2. By the law of total expectation, E[XY] = E[X * E[Y|X]] = E[X * X^2] = E[X^3]. Since X is symmetric about 0, all odd moments are zero: E[X^3] = 0. Therefore Cov(X, Y) = E[XY] - E[X]E[Y] = 0 - 0 = 0, giving correlation(X, Y) = 0.

questions.subject: prob
questions.q: Let A be a 5x5 matrix such that each element is i.i.d. Bernoulli(p = 0.50). The probability that the row-sum of the second row and the column-sum of the third column are both equal to 3 is: (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.s: Row 2 and Column 3 intersect at element A[2, 3] = b in {0, 1}. Case 1: b = 1 (prob 0.5). Remaining 4 elements in row 2 sum to 2: C(4, 2)(0.5)^4 = 6/16. Remaining 4 elements in col 3 sum to 2: 6/16. Prob = 0.5 * (6/16)^2 = 18/256. Case 2: b = 0 (prob 0.5). Remaining 4 elements in row 2 sum to 3: C(4, 3)(0.5)^4 = 4/16. Remaining 4 elements in col 3 sum to 3: 4/16. Prob = 0.5 * (4/16)^2 = 8/256. Total probability = (18 + 8)/256 = 26/256 = 13/128 ~= 0.1016 -> 0.10.

questions.subject: linalg
questions.q: Let A = (In - (1/n) * 1 1^T) be a matrix where 1 = (1, ..., 1)^T in R^n. The value of max_{x in S} x^T A x where S = {x in R^n | x^T x = 1} is: (Answer in integer)
questions.s: For unit vector x, x^T A x is the Rayleigh quotient of symmetric matrix A. By the Courant-Fischer theorem, its maximum over unit sphere S equals the largest eigenvalue of A. A is an orthogonal projection matrix onto the subspace orthogonal to 1, whose eigenvalues are 1 (with multiplicity n - 1) and 0 (with multiplicity 1). The maximum eigenvalue is 1.
